simple: The phone line carried the internet and phone calls at the same time, as tones too high to hear. A box with a modem inside sent Wi‑Fi to every room.
technical: DSL: ADSL2+ and then VDSL2 from street cabinets, from a few to tens of Mbit/s on the copper pair. A modem-router at home does NAT, with an 802.11n access point.

describe.simple: A laptop, open on the table. It’s on Wi‑Fi, with no cable: the box with the modem inside sings down the phone line.
describe.technical: A laptop on 802.11n Wi‑Fi to a DSL modem-router, which does NAT and sends DMT tones down the phone pair.

on-the-go.simple: Phones could watch videos now, over 3G. Everyone near the mast shared its radio waves, so a video came small, and sometimes it stopped to load.
on-the-go.technical: 3G with HSPA: HSDPA peaked at 7.2–14 Mbit/s, shared by the whole cell, and a phone got 1–3 Mbit/s in practice. NodeB → RNC → GGSN, with the packets in GTP-U tunnels; 360p was typical.

describe.simple: A phone with one round button under its screen, on 3G to a mast down the street.
describe.technical: A 2010 smartphone on HSPA (3G) to a NodeB, with the RNC and the GGSN behind it.

desk-2010.simple: The phone line carried the internet and phone calls at the same time, as tones too high to hear. At the desk, a cable ran from the laptop to the box with the modem inside.
desk-2010.technical: DSL: ADSL2+ and then VDSL2 from street cabinets, from a few to tens of Mbit/s on the copper pair. The laptop has a 100 Mbit/s Ethernet cable to the modem-router, which does NAT.

describe.simple: A laptop on the desk, with a cable to the box with the modem inside, which sings down the phone line.
describe.technical: A laptop on Ethernet to a DSL modem-router, which does NAT and sends DMT tones down the phone pair.
